title: const or let?
prompt:
Declare a constant `firstName` with the value `"Ada"`, and a `let` variable `score` starting at 0 that you then reassign to 42. Log both on one line using a template literal: `Ada: 42`.

Rules:
- `firstName` never changes — `const`.
- `score` is reassigned — `let`.
boilerplate: // Declare firstName and score, reassign score, then log them

tests.name: const firstName holds Ada
tests.hint: const firstName = "Ada"; — constants can't be reassigned.

tests.name: let score reassigned to 42
tests.code:
if (!/let\s+score\s*=\s*0\s*;/.test(code)) throw new Error("Start score at 0 with let.");
if (!/score\s*=\s*42\s*;/.test(code)) throw new Error("Reassign score to 42 (without const/let the second time).");
tests.hint: let score = 0; then later score = 42; — reassignment without a new declaration.

tests.name: template literal prints Ada: 42
